name: United States, California Vehicle Code (right-hand traffic)
status: validated by review: rules checked on CAT's 500 WOMD scenes by reading the trajectories and figures of every flagged crossing (see references/validation-us-california.md); the person's own labels were not used as ground truth
notes: 21800(a): at an all-way stop the first vehicle to arrive and stop goes first.

21800(b), 21801(a): on a tie (arrivals within 1 s) a left turn yields to oncoming traffic, otherwise the vehicle on the left yields to the one on the right. When both were already waiting when the clip began the order is unknown and no verdict is given: the one that goes first while the other waits is ordinary turn-taking, not evidence of a violation.
21802: at a two-way stop the vehicle at the sign yields to cross traffic.
21800(c): at a T junction without control the road that ends yields.

Uncontrolled junctions: only the left-turn rule is applied. First-entered and yield-right were tried and held for no more than chance on the 500 scenes, because the map usually lacks the signs or lights that really control such a junction.
A complete stop is required by law but is not used to label aggression: the clip starts mid-approach, so a stop before step 0 cannot be seen.
